A seed plant or spermatophyte (from Ancient Greek σπέρμα ( spérma ) ' seed ' and φυτόν ( phutón ) ' plant ' ; lit. ' seed plant ' ), [ 1 ] also called a phanerogam (taxon Phanerogamae ) or a phaenogam (taxon Phaenogamae ), is any plant that produces seeds . It is a category of embryophyte (i.e. land plant) that includes most of the familiar land plants, including the flowering plants and the gymnosperms , but not ferns , mosses , or algae .
